html:
Ismail I founded the Safavid dynasty and made Twelver Shia Islam the religion of Iran. He was crowned shah in Tabriz in 1501, at about fourteen.

He was the leader of the Safavid Sufi order, whose Turkmen followers, the Qizilbash or red heads, saw him as a holy figure. In a decade they took all of Iran. Ismail forced Sunni scholars to convert or leave and brought in Shia clerics from Lebanon and Iraq. He also wrote poetry in Turkish.

In 1514 the Ottoman sultan Selim I crushed his army at Chaldiran with guns. Ismail never led an army again. The Safavid state he built reached its height under Abbas the Great, and Iran remains the main Shia power.
